question: A 8-month-old girl is brought to her pediatrician because her mom is concerned that she may have a "lazy eye". She was born prematurely at 33 weeks and was 3 pounds at birth. Her mother also says that there is a history of visual problems that run in the family, which is why she wanted to make sure that her daughter was evaluated early. On presentation, she is found to have eyes that are misaligned both horizontally and vertically. Physical examination and labs reveal no underlying disorders, and the patient is discharged with occlusion therapy to help correct the misalignment. Which of the following would most likely have also been seen on physical exam?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Premature birth" -> "risk of strabismus" -> "misaligned eyes" -> "asymmetric corneal light reflex" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Family history of visual problems" -> "risk of strabismus" -> "misaligned eyes" -> "asymmetric corneal light reflex" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Premature birth" -> "risk of retinopathy of prematurity" -> "possible fundus neovascularization" -> 60%
analysis: The child in the scenario is likely experiencing strabismus, which is a condition where the eyes do not properly align with each other. This is supported by the description of misalignment both horizontally and vertically. A common finding in strabismus is an asymmetric corneal light reflex, which occurs when the reflection of light from a penlight is not centered on the pupils of both eyes, indicating misalignment. Other options such as bitemporal hemianopsia, increased intraocular pressure, fundus neovascularization, and nystagmus are not typically associated with strabismus in an infant. Bitemporal hemianopsia is related to optic chiasm issues, increased intraocular pressure is associated with glaucoma, fundus neovascularization is seen in conditions like retinopathy of prematurity or diabetic retinopathy, and nystagmus involves involuntary eye movements, which is not described in this case.
